answer: Cluster agents by shared fate. The ledger logs when each identity goes quiet and wakes up, and how its reply speed drifts. Like light through a prism, a farm splits into the same pattern: fifty accounts that all stall at dawn when one server reboots, or all slow to a whisper during one provider outage, get merged into a single reward share. To dodge this, an attacker must run each fake on separate hardware, network and schedule, which costs about as much as running real independent agents.
